cards.title: ICES-003, issue 7
cards.body: Issue 7 is dated 15 October 2020 and covers ITE and digital apparatus that generate or use timing at 9 kHz or more. Issue 6 or 7 was acceptable until 15 October 2021. After that, what is still being marketed meets issue 7.

cards.title: One limit set, one method
cards.body: Issue 7 dropped the alternative limits. You may still test to CAN/CSA-CISPR 32:17 or to ANSI C63.4, but not a mix of the two on one product. Say which one you used. Satellite outdoor units also follow Annex H, and they are measured to 18 GHz.

cards.title: Conducted table
cards.body: Class B matches the residential shape: a log slope from 0.15 to 0.5 MHz, then 56/46, then 60/50. Class A is 79/66, then 73/60. Both quasi-peak and average apply. If an external supply or a PoE injector feeds the product, measure at that device's AC mains.

cards.title: Radiated tables
cards.body: Table 2 is quasi-peak from 30 MHz to 1 GHz, at 3 m or 10 m, Class A and Class B. Above 1 GHz, Table 4 at 3 m is Class B 54 average / 74 peak and Class A 60 / 80, bandwidth at least 1 MHz. A different distance extrapolates at 20 dB/decade.

cards.title: How high, and the label
cards.body: Table 3 sets the top frequency from the highest internal frequency, up to five times that frequency and not past 40 GHz. The label looks like CAN ICES-003(A) / NMB-003(A) or the B form, not both. Wireless charging is RSS-216 while charging, and those emissions are not counted against ICES-003.

cards.title: Narrow exemptions
cards.body: Factory-installed vehicle electronics go to ICES-002. The same electronics added later do not. A fridge-door display and an external thermostat stay in ICES-003. So does anything that is not exclusively aircraft, utility, ISM, or one of the other listed cases. A multiunit product is exempt only if every piece is.

cards.title: ICES-002, issue 7
cards.body: Issue 7 (September 2020) covers vehicles, boats up to 15 m including outboard motors sold alone, and devices with a combustion engine or traction batteries. The transition ran to September 2022. CISPR 14-1 is not an ISED requirement, so a battery mower stays in ICES-002.

cards.title: Every unit, and who signs
cards.body: You cannot use the CISPR 12 statistical clauses to pass ICES-002. Each unit complies. Anyone who manufactures, imports, distributes, leases, offers, or sells can be responsible. A later modifier of a compliant truck picks up that duty for the modified product.

cards.title: Plugged-in vehicles
cards.body: Onboard switching supply is §4.3. An external supply is §4.4. Charge at 80% or more if you can set the current; otherwise keep the battery between 20% and 80%. Class B mains limits match the residential shape. Class A limits grow with rated power and carry installation conditions. Driving-mode radiated limits come from CISPR 12, which ICES-002 does not reprint.

cards.title: The ICES-002 label
cards.body: The plain example is CAN ICES-002 / NMB-002. If you used Class A limits in §4.3 or §4.4, the A has to appear. Class B may omit the letter. A compliant add-on stereo does not make the vehicle compliant. Annex K of the cited CISPR 16-1-1 is not an acceptable calibration path.
